note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Evaluation of a 3-day, severely painful headache with photophobia and intermittent visual phenomena; possible migraine-type headache; plan includes a neurological/eye exam and adjustments to analgesic therapy with follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Blinding headache started suddenly 3 days ago; constant and interfering with work; partial relief with ibuprofen.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia; occasional shooting lights; mild nausea without vomiting; no dizziness, weakness, numbness, or changes in smell/taste.
- Headache pattern: Persistent, present most of the time; ibuprofen provides some relief but does not fully resolve.
- Visual/neurologic symptoms: Light sensitivity; occasional visual phenomena described as “shooting lights”; no sustained vision changes reported; had an eye check recently with no vision changes.
- Negative findings: No fever, no nasal/cough symptoms, no weight loss, no night pain; no neurological deficits reported.
- Past medical history: Prior headaches in childhood; otherwise not else noted.
- Medications: The pill (oral contraceptive) started about a year ago; Ibuprofen as needed; Paracetamol; no other medications documented. Dose/route/frequency not documented for all meds.
- Allergies: Denies allergies.
- Social history: Lives alone; non-smoker; drinks alcohol; described as three drinks once a week.
- Relevant prior tests: Blood pressure checked in pharmacy a year ago (reported as normal); recent eye exam with reportedly no vision change.
- Plan for further assessment discussed: Neurological examination and fundoscopy; appointment recommended.

Examination:
- Not performed/not documented in transcript.
- Vitals: Not documented.

Impression:
- Working differential: Migraine-type headache suspected given photophobia and visual phenomena; persistent for 3 days without fever or systemic symptoms; absence of clear red flags documented in the transcript.

Plan:
- Schedule a full neurological examination and eye/fundoscopy (the doctor suggested booking via the support line; if symptoms settle sooner, appointment can be canceled).
- Medication plan: Prescribe a stronger NSAID equivalent to ibuprofen (name not specified) with advice to take with food; continue paracetamol as an adjunct; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Monitoring and safety: If the headache worsens, changes in character, or new symptoms (e.g., high fever, persistent focal deficits) occur, seek urgent care (A&E).
- Contraception review: BP will be checked during the examination; if migraine with visual symptoms persists, consider changing the pill.
- Follow-up/referral: No immediate specialist referral; arrange a consultation via the support team for the full exam and review of treatment; explore need for specialist referral after evaluation.

document_quality:
- Missing elements: Current vitals (BP, heart rate), full medication reconciliation with doses and routes, allergy status beyond “none,” no documented neuro exam or physical exam findings, no imaging or laboratory data obtained or ordered.
- Internal conflicts: None explicitly stated; transcript shows plan contingent on exam results.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear but some inaudible/unclear segments and filler words; overall adequate to extract plan and history.
